How to use this guide

Read one lesson, complete the action in your business, and keep the result somewhere you can find it. The examples are illustrations, not claims about real customers.

LESSON 01 / 05

Define what you're eligible for

Matching beats scrolling through every grant.

What to do

  1. Document location, sector, stage and relevant eligibility.
  2. Include accelerators, cohorts, pitch competitions, tenders and partnerships.
  3. Tag what evidence the business can provide today.

Example to adapt: describe what a real customer would do or see at this step. Use actual facts for your business.

LESSON 02 / 05

Choose credible sources

Aggregators can be outdated.

What to do

  1. Track verified official calls and organizational newsletters.
  2. Include SBDC, CDB, tourism bodies, Founder Institute and country-specific agencies where relevant.
  3. Record source URL, date checked and owner.

LESSON 03 / 05

Screen each opportunity

Not every headline deserves an application.

What to do

  1. Label opportunities VERIFIED OPEN, ANNOUNCED / VERIFY, CLOSED, or WATCHLIST.
  2. Check actual deadline and eligibility on the issuing organization's site.
  3. Log decision before investing hours in applications.

LESSON 04 / 05

Build an application pack

Good applications reuse accurate documents.

What to do

  1. Prepare business summary, pitch, financial records, registration documents and supporting evidence.
  2. Record the result in your workbook.
  3. Verify important details before treating the task as finished.

LESSON 05 / 05

Conduct a weekly opportunity review

Deadlines are missed when checking is sporadic.

What to do

  1. Record what changed, why it matters, which venture fits and next action.
  2. Use exact source and checked date for each opportunity.
  3. Never mark a deadline open from stale aggregator copy.
